free_tier.stated: No free tier. "WireGuard 38$ /Month" is the cheapest WireGuard entry; the only lower entry is L2TP at "32$".

egress.terms: No transfer allowance is published. The plan lists a rate: "100Mbps & Upgrade to 1Gbps", and "IPv4 Addresses: Available on Request".; ingress: tcp+udp

interface_detail: Client-configured tunnel; billing portal is a standard hosting cart.
tooling: wg-quick on the client's own router; L2TP, GRE and WireGuard are all offered
chaining: Only worth it if the client needs a custom block and BGP, which a free-tier VM cannot provide on its own.
binding_note: 100 Mbps carries about 32 TB in 30 days, so nothing binds at 1 TiB/month. The real weight is price: USD 38 for one tunnel is four to nineteen times the cheapest providers.

identity_cost.detail: Self-serve portal checkout, with purchase orders accepted: "Can I pay via a purchase order or for a full year in advance? Yes!". The signup form was not read.

reliability_note: Standard service is described as best-effort and month-to-month; no uptime figure is published for it.
confidence_note: Price, rate and options are first-party. Address count at the base price is not stated ("Available on Request"), which is the gap a sales email would close.

evidence.proved: WireGuard USD 38/month with custom IP allocations, 100 Mbps upgradeable to 1 Gbps, IPv4 and IPv6, BGP addon USD 10/month; month-to-month
"Static IP Anywhere" is aimed at hobbyists, small business, MSPs and enterprises; a 30 minute call is offered for enterprise sizing

price_per_tb_month: USD 38 per month for a WireGuard tunnel; USD 10 per month for a BGP session
notes: Enterprise tier is USD 99/month plus USD 279 setup with a 12-month minimum and a managed device; that tier is out of reach for a user but confirms the vendor ships real L2 handoff. Competitor GetAStatic's table lists Core Transit at "$38/mo (WireGuard)" and "Any port", which agrees with the vendor's own page. Not a free or nearly-free answer at any tier.

extras.wg_detail: The product is an encrypted tunnel with custom addressing, configured on the client's own router: "Encrypted Tunnels", "Bring Your Own Router", "Custom IP Allocations", "IPv4 & IPv6". A BGP session is a paid add-on at "$10 /Month".
extras.volume_stated: No transfer allowance is published. The plan lists a rate: "100Mbps & Upgrade to 1Gbps", and "IPv4 Addresses: Available on Request".
extras.transit_note: Core Transit routes the client's allocation from its own N+1 redundant network.
